hero.alt: Workers rebuilding a stone city wall at dusk while a watchman stands at the top.

hardDay.heading: Hard day? Start here.
hardDay.body:
If you're the anxious planner, hear this: your Father already knows what you need. You don't have to carry the whole future in your chest. If planning feels impossible this week, your task is honesty and one trusted believer.

Read "A Word to the Anxious Planner and the Frozen 'Truster.'"

If you are in danger, or you are having thoughts of not wanting to live, please stop here and reach out now. In the U.S., call or text 988, or call 911. Then tell a pastor or a trusted believer today.

bookRef.section: A Word to the Anxious Planner and the Frozen "Truster"

read.heading: Read first: Chapter 7
read.body:
Open to Chapter 7, "Wisdom Is Not Unbelief." Read "Planning Under Providence" and "Nehemiah: Prayer, Plans, and a Guard."

Nehemiah wept and prayed. Then he asked the king for letters and timber. He inspected the wall by night. He organized families to rebuild. He posted a guard. Prayer didn't cancel planning, and planning didn't cancel prayer.

If you've ever felt guilty for making a budget or a plan, like it meant you didn't trust God, this chapter is for you. Read it, then come back.

bookRef.section: Planning Under Providence; Nehemiah: Prayer, Plans, and a Guard

prompts: Have I treated planning, budgeting, or counsel as unbelief?

pulse.heading: The pulse: plan with open hands
pulse.body:
Wisdom is not the enemy of faith. Noah, Joseph, Nehemiah, and Paul all planned.

You plan, and God establishes. You say "if the Lord wills," and you still act. In the storm, Paul believed God's promise and still gave practical counsel to everyone on board. Hold the promise. Use the means.

bookRef.section: Planning Under Providence; Paul in the Storm: Promise and Practical Steps

verses.text: The heart of man plans his way, but the LORD establishes his steps.
Instead you ought to say, “If the Lord wills, we will live and do this or that.”

For this very night there stood before me an angel of the God to whom I belong and whom I worship, and he said, ‘Do not be afraid, Paul; you must stand before Caesar. And behold, God has granted you all those who sail with you.’

prompts: What plan needs open hands this week, held loosely and still acted on?

nameIt.heading: Name it: which one am I?
nameIt.body:
Chapter 7 names two people. The anxious planner, whose plans have become a rival god. And the frozen "truster," who uses faith as a cover for avoidance. Both need the same gospel.

The planner needs to seek the kingdom first and cast every care on God. The truster needs to write the plan and make the call. Be honest about which one you are this week.

bookRef.section: When "Faith" Becomes a Cover for Avoidance; When Planning Becomes a Rival God; A Word to the Anxious Planner and the Frozen "Truster"

verses.text: But seek first the kingdom of God and his righteousness, and all these things will be added to you. “Therefore do not be anxious about tomorrow, for tomorrow will be anxious for itself. Sufficient for the day is its own trouble.

do not be anxious about anything, but in everything by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known to God. And the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, will guard your hearts and your minds in Christ Jesus.
casting all your anxieties on him, because he cares for you.

prompts: Which am I this week: the anxious planner, or the frozen "truster"?
Where have I spiritualized delay and called it trust while today's clear duty waits?
Where has planning become a rival god for me?

build.heading: Build it: a one-page plan
build.body:
Wise faith prays and prepares, counts the cost, rests, and adjusts.

Make one plan, one page or less: the next step, the counsel you'll ask, and a date. Count the cost. Name what you'll have to stop. Then, once obedience is clear, pay it. Don't let the plan become the new place to hide.

bookRef.section: How Wise Faith Looks in Real Life; Counting the Cost Without Losing Heart

verses.text: For which of you, desiring to build a tower, does not first sit down and count the cost, whether he has enough to complete it? Otherwise, when he has laid a foundation and is not able to finish, all who see it begin to mock him, saying, ‘This man began to build and was not able to finish.’
The plans of the diligent lead surely to abundance, but everyone who is hasty comes only to poverty.
Do not boast about tomorrow, for you do not know what a day may bring.

prompts: The next step:
The counsel I'll ask (who and what):
The date:
The cost, and what I'll stop doing:

move.heading: Move: this week's practice
move.body:
From the end of Chapter 7:

Make one concrete plan under providence, one page or less: next step, counsel to ask, date. Pray "if the Lord wills," then take the first action within seven days.

The plan is a servant. The action is the point. If seven days pass, set a new date within three days.
prompts: I made a one-page plan
I prayed "if the Lord wills"
I took the first action within seven days
Missed it? New date (within three days):
move.cta: Close the app and go take your step

help.heading: Help: ask counsel, then own it
help.body:
Counsel is a gift, not a crutch. Ask for it. Then own the decision.

Bring your one-page plan to a trusted believer this week and ask, "What am I missing?" Then think of someone who's either drowning in plans or frozen without one, and offer to sit down with them for twenty minutes.

bookRef.section: Counsel Is a Gift, Not a Crutch

verses.text: Without counsel plans fail, but with many advisers they succeed.
Where there is no guidance, a people falls, but in an abundance of counselors there is safety.

prompts: Who I'll ask for counsel, and what I'll ask:
Someone I could sit down with (first name or initials):
help.cta: Send it, then put the phone down

pray.heading: Pray it: ask for wisdom
pray.body:
Wisdom is skill for living under God's rule. James says to ask God for it, and He gives generously without scolding. Asking in faith doesn't mean you never have questions. It means you come to Him with your whole heart, ready to follow what He shows you.

Father, I need wisdom for this: ____. You give generously, and You don't scold me for asking.

Here's my plan: ____. I hold it with open hands. If You will, I'll do this. Establish my steps. Amen.

verses.text: If any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask God, who gives generously to all without reproach, and it will be given him. But let him ask in faith, with no doubting, for the one who doubts is like a wave of the sea that is driven and tossed by the wind. For that person must not suppose that he will receive anything from the Lord; he is a double-minded man, unstable in all his ways.

prompts: Where I need wisdom:
My plan, in one line:

review.heading: Review: steward and child
review.body:
After your date, mark it: took the step, not yet, or holy wait.

Guardrail from Chapter 7, "What This Is Not": this isn't presumption. It isn't a ban on waiting. It isn't trust in techniques. And it isn't a denial that God does the supernatural. Unless the Lord builds the house, we labor in vain.

Plan as a steward. Trust as a child.

bookRef.section: What This Is Not; Plan as a Steward, Trust as a Child

verses.text: Unless the LORD builds the house, those who build it labor in vain. Unless the LORD watches over the city, the watchman stays awake in vain. It is in vain that you rise up early and go late to rest, eating the bread of anxious toil; for he gives to his beloved sleep.

prompts: How did it go? I took the step / Not yet, and I can name the block / Holy wait, and I can say why
What happened:
What did I need to adjust?
